sentences.text: 2] This is the first application filed by the applicant Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as she is apprehending her arrest in connection with private complaint No.5105/2024 pending before the Additional Sessions Judge, District Indore for the offence punishable under Sections 120-B, 420, 467, 468 and 471/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3] Allegation against the applicant is of fraud.

4] The case has arisen out of a private complaint f who was also issued notice on the last date of hearing, i.e., on 11.07.2025, and this Court, as an interim measure had also directed that no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant.

5] Counsel for the applicant, Shri Polekar has submitted that he has already furnished the copy in the Trial Court, and the respondent has the knowledge of the present case and the stay granted,
however, the notice could not be served on his address with the endorsement that the addressee is not known.
Thus, it is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25200 2 MCRC-29932-2025 submitted that under these circumstances, the notice may be deemed to be served.

6] On due consideration of submissions, on perusal of the documents filed on record, and taking note of the fact that the applicant has already filed the copy of the interim order in the Trial Court, of which the Smt. Nita vs Tikamchand on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102049599/
1 respondent is also aware of, and in such circumstances, it cannot be said that the respondent is not served in the present case, and in the absence is any objection, and further taking note of the fact that the date of transaction is also stated to be of 1994, this Court is of the considered opinion that the custodial interrogation of the applicant would not be necessary.
7 ] Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon her executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicant shall make herself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
She shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
8] Accordingly, MCRC stands allowed and disposed of.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Smt. Nita vs Tikamchand on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102049599/
